extension.summary: Browse and play your Jellyfin server media library.
extension.description: An addon to allow you to browse and playback your Jellyfin (https://jellyfin.org) Movie, TV Show and Music collections.
extension.news: v1:1.0.2-5 (2026-10-27): Fork of JellyCon 1.0.2 (twiebe) ------------------------------- + Show server errors to the user and let them resolve rejected logins + Don't keep Kodi from exiting: interruptible keepalive, faster service stop + Settings converted to settings format version 1 + Short help text for every visible setting + Context menu works again when Kodi started before the user logged in + A user switch is picked up right away, without restarting Kodi + Optionally save the password, so JellyCon signs in again by itself after the user was disabled + Playback, stop and the context menu react faster, background work no longer holds up the player + Resume starts at the resume point right away, without a second seek

extension.description:
Welcome to Jellyfin for Kodi! A whole new way to manage and view your media library. The Jellyfin addon for Kodi combines the best of Kodi - ultra smooth navigation, beautiful UIs and playback of any file under the sun, and Jellyfin - the most powerful fully open source multi-client media metadata indexer and server.
Jellyfin for Kodi is the absolute best way to enjoy the incredible Kodi playback engine combined with the power of Jellyfin's centralized database. Features: * Direct integration with the Kodi library for native Kodi speed * Instant synchronization with the Jellyfin server * Full support for Movie, TV and Music collections * Jellyfin Server direct stream and transcoding support - use Kodi when you are away from home!
extension.news: v1:2.2.0-5 (2026-10-27): Fork of jellyfin-kodi 2.2.0 (twiebe) ------------------------------------ + Update sync only writes the items that changed, fetched in parallel + Don't wipe the library when fetching its items fails + Don't sync a library twice after an interrupted sync + Page size setting is no longer silently limited to 50 + Faster sync: shared exit monitor, artwork settings read once, cached row class + Don't keep Kodi from exiting with the websocket, service restart works again + Roll back database changes when an error is raised + Keep the saved login when the server answers with an error + Close the progress dialog when a sync fails + Notify about new items after the first notification too + Honour the server offline notification setting + Keep the server's tracks when the transcode track dialog is disabled + Treat 0 days in next episodes as no limit again + Remove the enhanced artwork setting + Short help text for every visible setting + Add to playlist in the Jellyfin options of movies, episodes, music videos and songs + A stop no longer holds up other add-ons for 3 seconds (a skin's return to the info page) + Playback starts faster, the skip button and dialogs no longer hold up other add-ons + The stop position is reported to the second, not up to 10 seconds old + The skip button closes when seeking back before the segment + Optionally save the password, so jellyfin-kodi signs in again by itself after the user was disabled + "Update password" no longer stops library updates until Kodi restarts

extension.summary: Forks of the Jellyfin add-ons and the Nightcity skin
extension.description: Jellyfin for Kodi and JellyCon with fixes that are not released upstream yet. The add-ons keep their ids: install them from this repository once to replace the upstream versions, Kodi then takes their updates from here. Also the Nightcity skin for Kodi 21, which needs TMDb Helper.
A netrunner look in calm cyan with pink accents: cut corners, glitch titles and big artwork, with online movie and TV data from TMDb Helper.
extension.news: 0.4.77 - The music player's buttons come in the same order as the video player's: previous, play or pause, stop, next. With the quick menu shown, the top line dims as well, only the menu icon stays bright, and the page stays dimmed but visible after Back from the weather. Notifications have a white heading, yellow only for warnings and errors, a dimmed text under it, and thin outline icons: a circle for info, a triangle for a warning, an octagon for an error.[CR]0.4.76 - Every row on the home, movies, shows and music pages is numbered in pink before its title, 01 for the first row shown; hidden rows take no number. The genre tabs are as large as the row titles. In the music queue the playing track keeps its mark while the cursor moves: a dimmed blue bar in a track list, a line under the title on the cards. Right on the last music spotlight button moves on to the next album again, and the music queue has no progress line any more. After Back from a title page the cast and crew tabs switch on focus again.[CR]0.4.75 - The chevrons after the spotlight buttons sit at the usual gap after the last button.[CR]0.4.74 - Colours follow one guide: white for content, cyan for the cursor, a dimmed blue for state and hints, pink for the line above titles, dialog headings and the numbering in the settings and on the system page, yellow only for warnings. Notifications show an icon, and only warnings and errors have a yellow heading. Rating stars are grey, the mouse pointer is cyan. After the spotlight buttons three small chevrons, each a step darker, show that Right moves on to the next title.[CR]0.4.73 - The arrow after the spotlight buttons is a slim drawn chevron instead of a > sign.[CR]0.4.72 - A dim arrow right of the spotlight buttons, as tall as they are, shows that Right moves on to the next title.[CR]0.4.71 - The clock is white everywhere: on Home with the weather beside it, in the quick menu, on the startup screen and in the top line of the other windows.[CR]0.4.70 - During playback the title and plot of a movie or episode show its ratings, following the Ratings settings; an episode shows its own ratings, not the show's. The music player shows your own rating and the song and album ratings when there are any. The title and plot during playback have more room: the plot shows five lines before it scrolls.[CR]0.4.69 - Ratings have their own settings category: a switch per source, IMDb and Rotten Tomatoes critics on by default, and by default only the ratings TMDb Helper fetched for exactly that title, never the library's own. The spotlight keeps a title's ratings once they are fetched, also after the focus leaves or the spotlight comes back to it; a further setting fetches them without focus. On an episode page the ratings follow the focused episode. Ends at looks like the runtime next to it. Pink is now kept for the line above the titles: the shown tab, the selected value, counters, separators and clocks use a dark blue.[CR]0.4.68 - Switching between the home and movies pages keeps the spotlight on its title, and a new title in the spotlight crossfades its logo, poster and backdrop. Movie and episode pages and the spotlight show when playback would end, counted from the resume point, or the player's own end time for the title that is playing. They show every rating TMDb Helper has: IMDb with its Top 250 rank, TMDb, Rotten Tomatoes critics and audience, Metacritic, Trakt, Letterboxd and MDbList, or the library rating without it. Movie pages show resolution, HDR or SDR and the audio track too, and audio reads like DD+ 5.1; the info key during playback names them the same way. Playing music opens the player screen, and Back returns to where it started. The top line shows what plays and opens the player screen. The queue opens on the playing track, which carries a progress line, and a queue from one album is a plain track list. The tab underline fits the width of its text. On CoreELEC and LibreELEC the settings page links their settings add-on, and settings entries that showed no text show it again.[CR]0.4.67 - First music support: a Music page on Home with an album spotlight and rows, album and artist pages, the music library, a player screen and a music OSD with the queue. When the player controls close, the poster, title and plot go first and the controls follow. The shown tab is marked by a pink line under it instead of a pink triangle in front. The selected value in a list is marked by a slim pink bar at the left edge. Header lines separate their parts with a pink dot.[CR]0.4.66 - Back in the quick menu or on its icon closes the menu and returns to where you came from, also on the settings page. On a switch between home and movies the spotlight shows the new title at once: its logo no longer crossfades and the backdrop fades in with the page. The arrows after the genre in the spotlight are gone.[CR]0.4.65 - Switching between the home, movies and shows pages moves the spotlight on to the next title, so the two pages never show the same one after a switch. An episode page opened on a freshly started or slow box selects the right episode instead of the first one. Opening another info page after the title menu of a TMDb title no longer crashes Kodi.[CR]0.4.64 - On the home pages the held Home key, the S key and the power key move the cursor to the quick menu icon, which shows the quick menu; the same key again takes the cursor back. The player controls no longer hide by themselves while the cursor is in the chapter row, the cast row or anything below the controls. A subtitle, audio or video panel no longer stays on screen over the chapter row or the cast row.[CR]0.4.63 - With the cursor on the quick menu icon the quick menu is already shown: Down or OK enters it, Up from its top and Back return to the icon, Left and Right leave it. The player controls no longer hide by themselves while the cursor is in the subtitle, audio or video panel. When the player controls open, the controls appear first and the poster, title and plot follow a moment later.[CR]0.4.62 - The weather tile in the quick menu opens a weather page with the current conditions and the forecast for the next days. The player controls hide by themselves a while after the last key press, 8 seconds by default and 3 to 30 seconds in the new Player settings, and stay while the video is paused. The plot under the title in the player can be switched off.[CR]0.4.61 - The quick menu icon is a plain hamburger. Settings live in one place: the quick menu has a single Settings link to the settings page, which left the top menu and shows a System section with the machine facts and a Settings section with the settings groups.[CR]0.4.60 - On the way back in a cast and crew chain the page no longer shows the focus on its buttons for a second before it jumps to the person: the focus appears on the person once the list is in. During playback the cast row comes back at once, without the chapter row in between.[CR]0.4.59 - Back in a cast and crew chain returns to the person, film or show it was left from, on the same tab, instead of the top of the page. Up from a person opened during playback returns to the cast row on that person, not to the chapter row. An episode page reopened on the way back shows its own show again: the season tabs no longer list every show.[CR]0.4.58 - Down from above skips a row of tabs and lands on its content, Up reaches the tabs: genre rows, cast and crew, search results. Cast and crew tabs switch as soon as the cursor is on them, no OK needed. Episode info pages show resolution, HDR or SDR and the audio track. The skin settings pick the colour scheme. New add-on icon.[CR]0.4.57 - The skin settings open on the main menu, which now comes first and holds the glow switch under Effects. The Effects category and the separate Home pages entry in the settings are gone, Skin leads to the same page.[CR]0.4.56 - Up and Down on the number pad (PIN and number entry) keep the column, like on the keyboard.[CR]0.4.55 - The - and + of a setting with a value range drop their boxes and the pink: the selected sign sits on a small dark chip. The slider knob turns light instead of pink while it moves.[CR]0.4.54 - Down from Play on an episode lands on the episodes, past the season tabs; up from the episodes reaches them.[CR]0.4.53 - The quick menu links (Settings, System, Files) also work over an info page or a TMDb Helper chain: they close it first. The chapter cards show the start time once, under the picture.[CR]0.4.52 - The spotlight fades in on every switch between home and movies, also when both show the same movie. The chapter row shows Kodi's own chapter pictures in full cards when the Jellyfin server has none, instead of short cards without a picture.[CR]0.4.51 - The episode number stands before the title under the picture, where bright pictures no longer hide it. The top menu wraps around: left on home reaches the quick menu icon, right on it home again. A held Home key opens the quick menu also on remotes whose Home key Kodi knows as browser_home or home. The quick menu links the file manager (Files).[CR]0.4.50 - Up and Down on the keyboard keep the column: Down from e lands on d, not on the key that had the focus last in that row.[CR]0.4.49 - First public release. A calm cyberpunk skin for Kodi 21 with configurable home, movies and shows pages, info pages that walk top down, endless cast and crew navigation through TMDb Helper, a search page, a quick menu with clock, weather and power, and a player with track panels, chapter row and cast row.
